title: slottedIn counts a dry-published slot as placed, though a dry publication holds nothing
body:
## Summary
slottedIn reads a plan's slot part as placed when a slot for it is scheduled, publishing or published - including published DRY - while every other holder rule says a dry publication holds nothing.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/slots/read.ts:105 `SELECT 1 ... WHERE part_id = ? AND state IN ('scheduled', 'publishing', 'published')` has no `dry = 0`; its docstring (read.ts:98-103) defines placed as a slot that HOLDS its item. clashOf (core.ts:82) and the index slots_one_holder (schema.ts step 4) both say a dry-published slot holds nothing (the L62 ruling). So a project whose slot part went out only as a rehearsal reads its slot part ratified and the project shipped. Which is right is a product call: excluding dry makes a dry-launched project never ratify its slot part; keeping it makes 'shipped' mean 'rehearsed'.

## Flow
- compose + launch a project in dry mode, its slot part's slot published dry
- slottedIn -> true; the part reads ratified; listProjects groups the project 'shipped'

## Expected impact
The Projects shelf's 'shipped' group can hold projects nothing was published for. Could break: a dry rehearsal of a whole project that today completes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of 'holds an item' across the calendar
Before: 2 of 3 holder rules exclude a dry publication (clashOf, slots_one_holder); slottedIn does not
After: 3 of 3, or the docstring names the exemption
Method: probe - read the three rules; the behaviour is a direction choice, not a measurement
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: A stale slot claim the sweep cannot take over aborts the whole calendar pass
body:
## Summary
sweep's fenceOut throws `internal` when claimIn does not grant the take-over of a stale claim, and the sweep is one transaction, so every miss, drift and claim of that pass rolls back - every tick, until a person clears the lease.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/slots/sweep.ts:72-78 fenceOut: `if (o.kind !== "granted") throw new AppError("internal", ...)`; sweep.ts:104-151 applies every decision in one store.tx. claimStateIn judges staleness with lease-core staleReason; claimIn decides with decideClaim, which also weighs waiters in line (lease-core.ts sweepWaiters). If the two ever disagree (a waiter queued on slot:<id>, a holder judged gone by one and not the other), one unreclaimable lease freezes the calendar. Fixed: an interrupt that cannot fence out is skipped and reported (left publishing for the next pass) instead of aborting the pass.

## Flow
- a slot publishing under a dead holder, with a live waiter on slot:<id>
- tick: planSweep -> interrupt; fenceOut -> claimIn not granted -> throw
- the pass rolls back: no other slot is missed or claimed

## Expected impact
A calendar that silently stops going out, every tick red with the same internal error. Could break: nothing when the two judgements agree.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one bad claim costs that slot, not the calendar
Before: walked - one ungranted take-over aborts all N decisions of the pass
After: predicted - N-1 decisions land, the one slot is reported
Method: simulation - whether claimIn can refuse a take-over staleReason calls stale needs a seeded lease row with a waiter
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: vitest in slots.claim.test.ts: seed slot A publishing under DEAD with a live waiter row on slot:A, slot B overdue; sweep -> assert B is missed (control: today the sweep returns internal and B stays scheduled)

title: readQueue still selects each live job's quoted seconds one job at a time
body:
## Summary
After 0e55a9af readQueue reads every live job in one statement, then quotedSecondsOf issues one or two more per job (parts by job_id, then runs by job_id) and parses each record through its door.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/records/read.ts readQueue calls quotedSecondsOf(r, id) per row; packages/kernel/src/records/schema.ts:127-136 does `SELECT record FROM parts WHERE job_id = ?` and, on a miss, `SELECT record FROM runs WHERE job_id = ?`. Every receipt and every Plan read pays 1-2 statements per queued or running job. Fixed: one statement per table over the live job ids (IN list, chunked) into a map, or a LEFT JOIN in readQueue's own SELECT. data-access / batching-and-n-plus-one.

## Flow
- N live jobs on the queue
- planReceipt / readProject / listProjects -> readQueue -> N x quotedSecondsOf

## Expected impact
Statements per receipt drop from 1 + ~1.5N to ~3. Could break: a job served by neither a part nor a run must still read 0 s.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one statement per table instead of per job
Before: probe (reads-probe, 10 launched projects): planReceipt 13 statements, of which the per-job quote lookups grow with the queue
After: predicted constant in N
Method: simulation - the instrument exists (scratch reads-probe counting Reader.get/all); the batch touches schema.ts's shared helper
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: count Reader.get/all calls in planReceipt with 0 and with 50 live jobs (the round's reads-probe); better = the count is the same for both

title: launchOf rebuilds a kind's whole option table once per option it is asked about
body:
## Summary
pickRun, routeChoices and rerouteOptions filter modelOptions(kind) by calling launchOf per option, each of which rebuilds the kind's entries.

## Description
packages/kernel/src/records/launch.ts:193, :350, packages/kernel/src/records/reroute.ts:64; options.ts:121 launchOf -> entries(). (1 + k) table builds where 1 would do.

## Flow
- measured k per kind and the cost of one build

## Expected impact
None worth a change.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer option-table builds per receipt
Before: k <= 5 options per kind (still 5, frames 4); one modelOptions build 4.8 us (1000 builds of score: 4.8 ms)
After: saves at most ~5 builds = ~25 us per receipt, beside a SQLite transaction
Method: probe - timed modelOptions x1000 and counted options per kind
Result: not-better
Gate: none
evidence: score entries x1000 ms 4.8; options per kind max 5 (still)
